topic_ko: 한국에 온 교환학생이 존댓말 때문에 겪은 두 번의 실수와, 호칭어·발음을 둘러싼 문화 차이

passage: In Korea, showing respect is not merely good manners; it is built into the grammar itself.
An exchange student found that choosing the right level of politeness demanded constant attention.
At her home-stay family's table she answered her host father with a casual word instead of a polite one.
Only later did she learn that the situation had called for the respectful form.
In a lecture hall she asked her professor to explain again, but used the pronoun reserved for close friends.
Every head in the room turned toward her, and she froze without knowing why.
The professor, however, recognized that she was still learning and let the moment pass.
She remains puzzled by honorific words, yet expects that practice and advice will eventually make them natural.
choices: the reasons Korean grammar has become simpler over recent decades
the trouble a learner faces in handling Korea's language of respect
the advantages of studying abroad while living with a host family
the strategies professors use to correct students during lectures
the difficulty of translating polite expressions into English
theme.explanation_ko: 존댓말 선택의 어려움을 두 번의 실수로 보여 주고 마지막에 앞으로 익히겠다는 다짐으로 닫으므로 ②가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 문법이 단순해졌다는 서술은 없다. ③ 홈스테이는 실수의 배경일 뿐 유학의 장점을 다루지 않는다. ④ 교수는 이해해 주었을 뿐 교정 전략은 나오지 않는다. ⑤ 번역의 어려움이 아니라 사용의 어려움이다.

passage: Respect runs so deep in Korean culture that the language encodes it in every sentence ending.
A newly arrived student discovered how many choices that single fact forces on a speaker.
Answering her host father, she used the informal word rather than the respectful one.
The embarrassment came afterward, when someone explained which form she should have chosen.
A second slip followed in class, where she addressed her professor with an informal pronoun.
The whole room turned to look, and panic set in before she understood her mistake.
Her professor read the situation kindly and let her continue without comment.
Confusion has not disappeared, but she is confident that steady practice will settle it.
choices: 교수는 학생의 언어 실수를 반드시 지적해야 한다.
홈스테이 생활은 언어 학습에 가장 효과적인 방법이다.
한국 문화의 예절은 언어보다 행동에서 더 잘 드러난다.
외국인은 한국어의 문법 규칙을 끝내 익힐 수 없다.
존댓말은 혼란스럽지만 연습과 가르침으로 익힐 수 있다.
gist.explanation_ko: 혼란을 인정하면서도 연습과 도움으로 극복하겠다는 낙관으로 마무리되므로 ⑤가 요지이다.
gist.distractor_ko: ④ 끝내 못 익힌다는 비관은 본문과 반대이다. ① 교수는 오히려 지적하지 않고 이해했다. ② 홈스테이의 효과는 평가되지 않았다. ③ 행동보다 언어에서 드러난다는 것이 본문의 서술이다.

passage: Korean culture places respect at its center, and the language carries that value in its endings.
For an exchange student, every reply became a small decision about politeness.
She answered her host father casually and only later realized the form was wrong.
In class she used an informal pronoun for her professor and drew every eye in the room.
Panic followed, though the professor understood her position and moved on.
Commenters added that sibling terms in Korea are used for older friends as well.
One noted that a Korean word for an older brother sounds like the German word for grandfather.
Honorifics still confuse her, but she believes practice and guidance will win in the end.
choices: Living with a Host Family: A Guide
How to Master German in a Year
The History of Korean Family Names
title.explanation_ko: 예의를 갖추려다 오히려 어려움에 빠진 경험이 글 전체를 관통하므로 ③이 제목으로 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ④ 독일어는 댓글의 발음 비교로만 나온다. ⑤ 성씨의 역사는 다루지 않는다. ① 강의 폐지 주장은 없다. ② 홈스테이 안내서가 아니다.

passage: Korean honorifics demand that a speaker weigh age, rank, and closeness before every reply.
An exchange student answered her host father with a word meant for friends.
She learned only afterward that the polite form had been required.
Later, in a lecture hall, she used an informal pronoun for her professor.
The moment I uttered it, everyone turned around and looked at me.
She panicked, unsure of what she had done wrong.
The professor understood her situation and let the class continue.
She still finds honorifics confusing, but she expects to master them with practice.
implication.underlined: The moment I uttered it, everyone turned around and looked at me.
choices: The whole class instantly noticed that something had gone wrong with her words.
The students had been waiting for her to speak up during the discussion.
Her classmates were impressed by how fluently she spoke Korean.
The lecture had already ended, so everyone was preparing to leave.
She had spoken so quietly that people turned to hear her better.
implication.explanation_ko: 모두가 동시에 돌아본 것은 그 말이 어법상 크게 어긋났음을 즉시 알아챘다는 뜻이므로 ①이 적절하다.
implication.distractor_ko: ② 발언을 기다렸다는 서술은 없다. ③ 감탄이 아니라 당혹의 반응이다. ④ 수업이 끝났다는 언급이 없다. ⑤ 목소리 크기의 문제가 아니라 호칭의 문제이다.

passage: Respect is a big thing in Korean culture, and it shows even in their language.
There are simply so many things that a foreign speaker must consider before answering.
My first embarrassing moment took place when my host father asked me to tell his wife to come for dinner.
I was embarrassed to learn that I should have said the polite form in that situation.
When I didn't hear the professor clearly, I used the pronoun that friends use with each other.
The moment I uttered it, everyone turned around and looking at me in surprise.
Luckily, the professor understood my situation and explained the point again.
I'm still confused about honorific words, but I'm sure practice will help me.

underlines.text: that a foreign speaker must consider

grammar.explanation_ko: and 로 앞의 과거형 turned 와 병렬 연결되는 자리이므로 looking 이 아니라 과거형 looked 여야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① consider 의 목적어가 빠진 목적격 관계절이라 옳다. ② ask 는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취한다. ③ 과거에 대한 후회이므로 should have p.p. 가 맞다. ⑤ 감정을 느끼는 주체가 사람이므로 confused 가 옳다.

passage: Respect is a big thing in Korean culture, and it shows even in the way people speak.
Korean honorifics are very confusing for someone who has just arrived.
My first embarrassing moment took place at my home-stay family's dinner table.
I responded to my host father's request with the word friends use with each other.
Another uncomfortable situation occurred in a classroom a few weeks later.
When I could not hear the professor clearly, I asked him to repeat his words politely.
The moment I uttered it, everyone turned around and stared at me in silence.
Luckily, the professor understood my situation, and I panicked only for a moment.
vocab.explanation_ko: 글쓴이는 교수에게 친구 사이에나 쓰는 호칭을 썼기 때문에 소동이 벌어졌으므로, politely 는 문맥상 informally 가 되어야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① 존댓말이 헷갈린다는 서술로 자연스럽다. ② 창피했던 순간이라는 흐름에 맞다. ④ 모두가 돌아보고 응시했다는 묘사로 적절하다. ⑤ 다행이라는 서술과 이어지므로 옳다.

passage: Korean culture treats respect as something the language itself must carry.
An exchange student answered her host father with a casual word instead of a polite one.
She only learned afterward which form the moment had required.
Later she used a friend's pronoun for her professor, and the whole lecture hall turned to stare.
She panicked, but her professor read the situation and let it go.
Looking back, she realized that her mistakes came less from bad grammar than from ______________________.
Verb endings can be memorized, but the social judgment behind them takes far longer to build.
Still, she is confident that practice and guidance will get her there.
choices: the shortage of Korean speakers willing to correct foreigners
a stubborn refusal to study the textbook rules she was given
the professor's habit of speaking far too quickly in lectures
not yet sensing where each listener stood in relation to her
her decision to live with a host family rather than in a dorm
blank.explanation_ko: 빈칸 뒤에서 '어미는 외울 수 있지만 그 뒤의 사회적 판단이 오래 걸린다' 고 밝히므로, 상대와의 관계를 아직 감지하지 못했다는 ④가 적절하다.
blank.distractor_ko: ② 공부를 거부했다는 서술은 없다. ③ 교수의 말 속도는 강의실 일화의 계기일 뿐 실수의 원인이 아니다. ⑤ 홈스테이 선택은 원인으로 제시되지 않았다. ① 교정해 줄 사람이 없었다는 언급은 없다.

irrelevant.explanation_ko: ④는 지하철 시설에 관한 진술로, 존댓말 실수담이라는 글의 흐름과 무관하다.

order.given: Respect is a big thing in Korean culture, and it shows even in the language itself. For a newly arrived exchange student, Korean honorifics were very confusing, because there were simply so many things to consider.

blocks.A: A second uncomfortable situation occurred in a classroom. Unable to hear the professor clearly, she asked him to explain again, but used the pronoun that friends use with each other.
blocks.B: Her first embarrassing moment took place at the dinner table, when her host father asked her to call his wife. She answered with a casual word, and learned only afterward that the polite form had been required.
blocks.C: Every student turned around to look at her, and she panicked. Luckily, the professor understood her situation, and she left the room determined to get the hang of honorifics.

order.explanation_ko: 존댓말이 어렵다는 도입(주어진 글) → 첫 실수인 식탁 일화(B) → 두 번째 실수인 강의실 일화(A) → 그 결과와 다짐(C) 순이 자연스럽다.
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 'A second uncomfortable situation' 은 첫 번째 사례(B)가 나온 뒤여야 성립하고, (C)의 '모두가 돌아보았다' 는 (A)의 발화에 대한 반응이므로 (A) 바로 뒤에 와야 한다.

summary.summary_template: Repeated __(A)__ with Korean honorifics left the writer flustered in front of others, but she remains __(B)__ that steady practice will let her use them naturally.
summary.explanation_ko: 존댓말에서 거듭 '실수' 했지만 연습으로 익히리라 '기대' 한다는 흐름이므로 missteps–hopeful 이 적절하다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그저 고려해야 할 것이 너무나 많다.
writing.answer: There are simply so many things to consider.
writing.explanation_ko: There + be 구문의 진짜 주어는 so many things 이고, to consider 는 그 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미는 to부정사의 형용사적 용법이다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 또 다른 불편한 상황이 강의실에서 일어났다.
writing.answer: Another uncomfortable situation occurred in a classroom.
writing.explanation_ko: another 뒤에는 단수명사가 오고, occur 는 자동사이므로 수동태로 쓰지 않는다.

writing.question: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.context: The writer used a casual word to her host father and an informal pronoun to her professor, so both mistakes came from choosing the wrong level of ___________.
writing.explanation_ko: 두 실수 모두 상대에 맞는 '공손함' 의 수준을 잘못 골라 생긴 것이므로 politeness 가 적절하다. (respect 도 가능)

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: I'm still confused about honorific words, but with practice and guidance, I'm sure I will get the hang of it.
writing.answer: 나는 여전히 존댓말에 대해 혼란스럽지만, 연습과 가르침이 있다면 반드시 그 요령을 터득하게 될 것이라고 확신한다.
writing.explanation_ko: confused 는 감정을 느끼는 사람에게 쓰는 형태이고, get the hang of 는 '요령을 터득하다' 라는 관용 표현이다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.summary: The writer is still __(A)__ about honorific words, but believes that practice and __(B)__ will help her use them correctly.
writing.explanation_ko: 마지막 문장에서 글쓴이는 여전히 confused 하다고 밝히면서 practice and guidance 를 극복의 조건으로 든다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 이 글의 주제문을 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
conditions: honorifics 와 confusing 을 반드시 포함할 것
writing.answer: Korean honorifics are confusing for foreign learners, but practice and guidance can make them natural.
writing.explanation_ko: 존댓말의 어려움과 연습을 통한 극복이라는 두 축을 한 문장에 담으면 된다.
